title: Design: Late-month invoice is still due the next month
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure a work order was invoiced with the invoice date Oct 28, 2026, for a customer who holds the shop's own term due on day 10 of the following month.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Open the attached design picture ct-p9-03-invoice-oct-28-still-due-nov-10.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
  • Start on that work order.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "Finance" tab.
  2. Resize the browser window to 1536 px wide (for example, maximise it on a 1536 x 864 screen at 100% zoom).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The invoice lines read "Invoice date: Oct 28, 2026" and "Due date: Nov 10, 2026" (as in ct-p9-03-invoice-oct-28-still-due-nov-10.png).

Step 2:

  • At 1536 px nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off and nothing needs a sideways scroll.
  • The layout described above is unchanged, only wider.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R2: “A "day of the following month" term is always due in the month after the invoice date, whatever the day of the invoice: with day 10, an invoice dated Oct 5 and one dated Oct 28 are both due Nov 10.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Default Credit Terms" (https://claude.ai/artifact/2erYxWz2ffDNcoXzEfu6wf), read 23 Oct 2026: page "9 Invoice due date" ("Invoice Oct 28: still due Nov 10"). Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the PRD quotes, except where this held design case follows the design.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ct-p9-03-invoice-oct-28-still-due-nov-10.png

The design's own words:

  • “Always the next month, even when the 10th of this month is still ahead or nearly here. Day 31 in a 30-day month uses its last day (Nov 30).”
